title: When the goal is years away: renew
objectives: Explain the renew-versus-hold decision with illustrative numbers.
Say why renewal should usually come with a step-up.
body_md:
Decision point five is where most value is quietly lost. The SIP ends, the instalments stop, and nobody calls.

## The illustration

₹10,000 a month for 10 years, at an assumed 12% a year, is worth about ₹23.2 lakh at year 10.

- Hold for 10 more years without a SIP: about ₹72.2 lakh at year 20.
- Renew and continue for 10 more years: about ₹99.9 lakh at year 20.

The existing units compound either way. Renewing adds the extra years of contributions, and those contributions are what close the gap.

## Why renew with a step-up

A flat renewal repeats the amount that was right ten years ago. Income has usually grown and costs certainly have. Renewing with a 5–10% step-up keeps the new instalment in line with today's salary rather than yesterday's.

## Renewal mechanics

- Renew before the old tenure ends, so there is no gap in debits.
- Check the AMC's renewal terms; a renewal may be treated as a fresh registration.
- Update the bank mandate if the new amount is higher.
- Put the new end date in the review calendar immediately.
example: Anil's SIP ended at ₹23.2 lakh, with eight years to the college goal. Renewing at the same amount reaches about ₹99.9 lakh over a full 20 years; he renews with a 10% step-up instead of a flat amount.
say: The units keep compounding whether or not you renew; the renewal adds the contributions.
Let's renew at today's income, not at the amount that was right ten years ago.
never: Holding and renewing give the same result.
Renewal is automatic, so there is nothing to plan.

talk_track.title: Renew or just hold?
talk_track.text: At year ten, the SIP is worth about twenty-three lakh. If the client simply holds for ten more years, it grows to about seventy-two lakh. If the client renews the SIP for those ten years, it reaches about one crore. The existing units compound either way; renewing adds the extra years of contributions. And many investors simply forget to renew, so put the end date in the review calendar.

check.q: ₹10,000 a month for 10 years, then 10 more years: what does the illustration show?
o: About ₹72.2 L if held; about ₹99.9 L if renewed
About ₹99.9 L if held; about ₹72.2 L if renewed
check.why: Holding reaches about ₹72.2 L; renewing reaches about ₹99.9 L, because renewal adds ten more years of contributions.

check.q: Why renew with a step-up rather than a flat amount?
o: Because the flat amount was right ten years ago, and income and costs have moved since
Because a step-up removes the exit load
Because a step-up guarantees the goal
check.why: The old instalment is a smaller share of today's income, and a step-up keeps the renewal realistic.

check.q: What must be checked before a renewal with a higher amount?
o: The bank mandate and the renewal terms
check.why: A higher instalment needs a mandate that covers it, and renewal terms can differ from the original registration.
